page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.xlarge is a compute-oriented virtual server powered by the KVM hypervisor on x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The CPU implementation includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI. The instance is paired with 4.0 GB of system memory, reflecting a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage is included, and no hardware GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark outcomes locate the instance primarily within lower-tier performance ranges across compute and memory subsystems. In PassMark testing, the server achieved a CPU mark of 3646.62 and a memory score of 1229.28. Geekbench scores recorded 984.0 for single-core and 2207.0 for multi-core evaluations. Memory bandwidth measurements show 164.26 GB/sec for small cached blocks (16 KB), reducing to 20.87 GB/sec read and 18.81 GB/sec write on uncached 256 MB blocks. Synthetic throughput benchmarks reflect 19.26 GB/sec for single-threaded gzip compression, alongside Redis set performance reaching 2.88 million operations per second and static web serving throughput of 3.47 GB/sec. Language model inference on small 135M parameter models delivered 239.2 prompt tokens per second and 67.57 generation tokens per second.

The 1:1 memory-to-core ratio represents a deliberate architectural tradeoff, prioritizing raw core allocation over capacity for memory-resident datasets. Combined with reliance on remote block storage due to the absence of local disks, the server provides an entry-level compute footprint. It is suited for lightweight compute tasks, small batch jobs, basic microservices, static web delivery, and CI/CD worker nodes that do not exceed the 4.0 GB memory ceiling.
